title: Alpaca Secures MAS In-Principle Approval to Launch Brokerage Services in Singapore
summary: Alpaca Singapore has received in-principle approval from MAS for a CMS license to offer brokerage and custodial services in Southeast Asia.
body_markdown:
We’re excited to announce that our Southeast Asian headquarters, Alpaca Securities Pte. Ltd. (“Alpaca Singapore”), has received in-principle approval (IPA) from the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) for a Capital Markets Services (CMS) license, marking another milestone in Alpaca’s global expansion.


The IPA advances Alpaca’s strategy to deepen its presence in Southeast Asia and support financial institutions across the region through a locally regulated Singapore entity. Once licensed, Alpaca Singapore plans to provide brokerage and custodial services and serve as a local counterparty to prospective partners.


“As financial institutions across Southeast Asia look to meet growing customer demand for international investing, Singapore is a natural hub for connecting the region’s investors to global markets,” said Rohit Mulani, President of Alpaca Southeast Asia. “This milestone strengthens our ability to support institutions locally with global brokerage infrastructure, regional expertise, and a strong regulatory foundation. We’re excited to help our partners expand the markets and investment products available to their customers and shape the next era of investing across Southeast Asia.”


Singapore is a strategic hub for Alpaca’s operations and continued growth across Southeast Asia, supported by an[established local team led by industry veteran](https://alpaca.markets/blog/alpaca-welcomes-rohit-mulani-and-david-grant-as-new-southeast-asia-leaders/) , David Grant, CEO of Alpaca Singapore.


Alpaca’s expansion in Singapore is grounded in the same commitment to regulatory compliance that underpins its infrastructure globally and builds on its broad regulatory footprint, which spans the US,[UK](https://alpaca.markets/blog/alpaca-enters-uk-and-eu-market-through-wealthkernel-acquisition/) ,[30 countries across the European Economic Area (EEA)](https://alpaca.markets/blog/alpaca-completes-eea-passporting-to-29-countries-expanding-access-to-regulated-investment-services-across-europe/) , Japan,[India](https://alpaca.markets/blog/alpaca-enters-indias-gift-city-broker-dealer-market-through-zincmoney-ifsc-acquisition/) , and The Bahamas. Across these markets, Alpaca supports fintechs and financial institutions with locally regulated access to its brokerage infrastructure. Today, Alpaca serves partners in more than 50 countries worldwide.


Read more about our[APAC presence and expansion](https://alpaca.markets/blog/alpaca-partners-with-indonesia-stock-exchange-to-enable-cross-border-market-access-via-paln/) .

Interested in learning more about how you can build with Alpaca’s brokerage infrastructure in Southeast Asia?

For existing partners, please contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) or email the Success team at[\[email protected\]](https://alpaca.markets/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#90f3e5e3e4fffdf5e2e3e5f3f3f5e3e3d0f1fce0f1f3f1befdf1e2fbf5e4e3) .


---


*An in-principle approval (IPA) reflects MAS' view that a licence may be issued to the applicant upon the fulfilment of specified conditions and provided there are no material adverse developments affecting the applicant. An IPA does not constitute a licence for Alpaca Securities Pte. Ltd. to provide brokerage and custodial services at this juncture. MAS reserves the right to rescind the IPA in circumstances where it considers appropriate.*
